question: Which prediction-path mechanism explains why the R13 guided fixed-budget allocation gains 5 code hits but loses 10 technical-prose hits versus equal allocation?
hypothesis: Replay R13 exactly: same three leave-one-domain-out arms, 15,819 non-target training bytes per arm, 256 motifs, sealed 582-byte evaluation prefixes, 872-byte adaptation reservoirs, and the exact EQUAL and GUIDED allocations. Add attribution only. For every sealed evaluation position, compare EQUAL and GUIDED predictions and assign exactly one frozen category: motif_admission_in_guided, motif_eviction_in_guided, motif_successor_refinement, baseline_byte_refinement, or prediction_unchanged. Record signed hit delta GUIDED_correct-EQUAL_correct. Category sums must reconstruct code=+5, structured=0, technical_prose=-10 and aggregate=-5 exactly. The dominant technical-prose loss mechanism is the category with the most negative prose signed delta. No allocation, budget, capacity, predictor, source, evaluator, or authority change is allowed.

attribution.dominant_loss_rule: technical-prose category with most negative signed hit delta

classification_rules.supported: valid with exact accounting and one category explains at least 50% of the absolute technical-prose loss
classification_rules.mixed: valid with exact accounting and at least one category has negative prose contribution but none reaches 50%
classification_rules.negative: valid but no frozen category explains a negative prose contribution despite replayed loss
classification_rules.invalid: any identity, authority, source, budget, split, allocation, category accounting, determinism, provenance, or capacity requirement fails

successor_if_supported.intent: measure preregistered per-domain marginal value curves around the fixed R13 budget without selecting a new policy from the same data

successor_if_mixed_or_negative.intent: factor interacting admission/refinement effects before any new allocation policy

no_post_result_tuning_rule: Do not alter R13 data, allocations, budgets, predictor, categories, accounting targets, 50% criterion, classification, or authority after primary output.
